analysis: Examined all five changed files. (1) GPTOSSHarmonyTemplateFixes.swift:45-47 adds a static CBv2StopStringScope that restricts client stop-string matching to the Harmony final channel (opener `<|channel|>final`, `<|message|>`, closers `<|end|>`, `<|return|>`, `<|call|>`, `<|start|>`). ModelEOSPolicy.swift:29-36 exposes it through ChatTemplateFixes.stopStringScope. This is request-semantics logic with no new data egress, key handling, or attestation. The scope only narrows where consumer-supplied stop strings match. A consumer can already control its own stop strings, so this introduces no cross-tenant channel and no change to cache scoping (T-041). The scope runs inside the engine after decryption, and the plaintext handling boundary is unchanged (TB-007). Residual risk is availability or correctness only: an unterminated final channel could mean stops never match, but max_tokens and the EOS tokens still bound generation (T-010, T-029). The EngineV2Bridge, ChatTemplateFixes and CBv2 engine implementations are not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify the matcher. The bridge tests added at EngineV2BridgeTests.swift:807-838 cover the main cases. (2) JSONAnswerFormat.swift:81 only adds `.logprobs` to the ignored event cases in an exhaustive switch. Logprobs are not appended to the validated content, so the JSON validation is unaffected. I did not verify whether logprobs get exposed elsewhere; that is outside this diff. (3) ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift:249 maps the new `.responseFormatCutOffByMaxTokens` case to 422. This is needed for an exhaustive switch. The sanitized failure path still carries no generated content. The case is not handled in boundedInferenceErrorReason or inferenceFailureCode, but those fall through to the status switch (422 maps to invalidRequest) without content leakage. The bridge, translation and MLXLMServer dependencies are external to the supplied evidence, so the new request plumbing (`stopStringScope` into `cbv2Request`) is unverified. No security regression identified.
